jyutping: jau5 di1 je5 m4 hou2 gong2 dak1 taai3 baak6
meaning: some things shouldn’t be said too directly
usage: This phrase is used when advising someone to be cautious about expressing certain information too plainly.
It suggests that some matters are better left implied or hinted at rather than clearly stated.
The expression is often used in sensitive situations or when dealing with delicate topics.
It can serve as a subtle reminder to consider the feelings or reactions of the listener before speaking too frankly.
This phrase reflects the cultural preference for indirectness in communication, especially in complex social contexts.
